en: Pre-training and post-training are 2
important terms and concepts related to the
training part of an AI model.
Pre-training is about building the model's
broad underlying capabilities from a very
large dataset. So for example, for large
language models, typically simply the entire
text you could find in the legal internet.
That is what would go into pre-training. You
would use all that data to build that neural
network that's able to predict text.
Post-training then, as the name suggests,
builds up on that neural network and shapes
the behavior, the specialization, the
reasoning capabilities, the safety of that
neural network. So the neural network that
comes out of pre-training is
pretty raw, and it's also not a good
assistant because all it is able to do is
predict text based on input.
Coming from the internet, which of course
means there's a lot of weird stuff in there.
And it most importantly means that it's not
really optimized to act as an assistant.
If you would ask a raw pre-trained model a
question,
it might just answer with another question
or by simply spitting out another question
mark because in its training data, it didn't
necessarily see that every question gets an
answer. Not every question in the internet
gets an answer after all.
Well, it's training where experts at these
AI companies then add more
artificially generated training data to the
training set to fine-tune the model to, for
example, understand that for a question it
should produce an answer but not an endless
amount of answers, that answers should be
friendly and helpful, that it should decline
certain requests. For example, if you ask it
to build a bomb, that it should not do that.
That's the part that happens in
post-training. Commonly and often also
referred to as fine-tuning.
